rationale: Prior to 2022, only a small number of individuals with pathogenic BRD4 variants or microdeletions encompassing BRD4 had been identified (including the initial reports by Olley et al. 2018 and interstitial 19p13.12 deletion cases reported by Alesi et al. 2019, totaling fewer than 10-15 published individuals). The delineation by Jouret et al. (2022) characterized an international cohort of 14 newly identified individuals (including two fetuses). When integrated with the initial cohorts and subsequent reviews (such as Lonardo et al. 2025 and Ascaso et al. 2024), the cumulative number of molecularly and clinically confirmed individuals with BRD4-related Cornelia de Lange syndrome 6 (CDLS6; OMIM #620568) documented in the international medical literature clearly exceeds 20.

evidence.text: Jouret et al. assembled an international collaborative cohort describing 14 new patients (including two fetuses) with BRD4-related disorder, representing the first major multi-patient cohort study dedicated to this cohesinopathy subtype.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We formed an international collaborative study, and collected 14 new patients, including two fetuses. We report the first cohort of patients with BRD4-related disorder and delineate the dysmorphic features at different ages.

evidence.text: Lonardo et al. performed a comprehensive literature review synthesizing atypical and non-classic CdLS cases associated with BRD4 alterations, capturing cases from Olley et al., subsequent deletions, and the Jouret et al. cohort.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for cardinal CdLS dysmorphic features (e.g., synophrys, microcephaly, upper-limb reduction defects) specifically in BRD4 intragenic variant carriers versus 19p13.12 microdeletion carriers across all published cases?
new_directions.rationale: Contiguous gene deletions at 19p13.12 involve other genes like NOTCH3 and AKAP8, which may introduce confounding phenotypic features not attributable purely to BRD4 haploinsufficiency.

new_directions.question_text: Can international cohesinopathy registries establish consensus clinical scoring thresholds to reliably distinguish CDLS6 from classic NIPBL-related CdLS and Coffin-Siris spectrum before molecular testing?
new_directions.rationale: Because CDLS6 often presents as an 'atypical' or milder CdLS phenotype, differentiating discriminating facial and limb features quantitatively from other cohesinopathies is vital for prompt diagnostic recognition.
